title: Difficulty Level Recognition
tagline: Year 4 — Judging at first glance how hard a question is, using steps, topics combined and size of numbers

introduction.overview: Good test-takers can tell in a few seconds how hard a question will be. This chapter gives a simple scoring rule you can apply at first glance: count the steps, add 2 for each extra topic combined, add 1 if the numbers are large or awkward. A score of 3 or less is Easy, 4 to 6 Medium and 7 or more Hard. The rule is a training device, not a law: it helps you decide order and time. The rules and figures used in examples are hypothetical teaching rules, not the policy of any real company or platform.
introduction.placementRelevance: Recognising difficulty quickly is the basis of triage and of the skip decision.
introduction.realWorldContext: Estimating effort before starting a task is a standard professional skill.

learningObjectives: Count steps and topics at first glance
Map the score to a band and a time budget
Spot trap features that hide difficulty
Calibrate the rule against your own timings

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Difficulty score = steps + 2 × (topics − 1) + 1 if large numbers. Bands: ≤3 Easy, 4–6 Medium, ≥7 Hard.

coreDefinitions: Step: one distinct calculation or deduction.
Topic: a different area combined in the question.
Large numbers: numbers that make arithmetic slow.
Calibration: adjusting the rule to your timings.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Difficulty is mostly about the number of things you must hold in your head.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Count steps, count topics, check numbers, add, and read the band.

mainNarrative: "Find 20% of 450": one step, one topic, ordinary numbers: score 1, Easy, about 20 seconds.
"A shop gives successive discounts of 20% and 10% on ₹750 and then adds 5% tax": three steps, one topic: score 3, Easy-to-Medium boundary, about 60 seconds.
"Two pipes and a leak fill a tank; the leak starts after 2 hours": four steps, one topic with a phase change: score 4 or 5, Medium.
"Mixture of alloys sold at a profit with a discount": three or four steps and two topics (mixtures, profit): 4 + 2 = 6, Medium to Hard.
A word problem with large awkward numbers adds 1 and often 20 seconds.

deepDiveAspects.title: Hidden topics
deepDiveAspects.content: A "percent" question that needs a ratio is two topics; count both.

deepDiveAspects.title: Wording length
deepDiveAspects.content: Long wording does not make a question hard unless it adds steps.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Score = steps + 2 per extra topic + 1 for large numbers; ≤3 Easy, 4–6 Medium, ≥7 Hard.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Hard questions are the first to skip.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Tag difficulty on every mock question.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The rule is a training aid.
